title: Attempt report, family 1
description: What one execution attempt did, as the engine reports it (AttemptReport.to_dict). It has no schema_version of its own: it is versioned through the plan document that embeds it in last_finalized_execution.report, and the plan_status snapshot copies parts of it. The report describes plans that were malformed too, so step_ids, unreached_step_ids and failure_policy keep the values the plan gave.

plan_generation.description: The generation captured with the execution request; null when the caller captured none.

run_token.description: The run token captured with the execution request; null when the caller captured none.

failure_policy.description: The policy the attempt ran under, as recorded: a plan with an unknown or malformed policy is rejected, and its report keeps the value it gave.

step_ids.description: The plan's step IDs in plan order, exactly as the plan gave them: an entry need not be a string when preflight rejected the plan.

step_outcomes.description: The terminal outcome of each step that reached one, by step ID.

unreached_step_ids.description: The planned steps with no outcome, in plan order, exactly as the plan gave them.

failures.description: How each failed step failed, by step ID.

direct_blockers.description: For each blocked step, the failed or blocked prerequisites that blocked it.

failed_ancestors.description: For each blocked step, every failed step upstream of it.

diagnostic.description: An attempt-level failure not attributable to one step.

publication_failure.description: Why the report could not be published, when it could not.

timestamp.description: An RFC 3339 date-time in UTC, ending in Z: to the whole second, such as 2026-10-22T10:00:00Z, or with a fraction of one to six digits whose last digit is not 0, such as 2026-10-22T10:00:00.25Z.

outcome.description: The overall outcome of an attempt.

step_outcome.description: The terminal outcome of one step within one attempt.

step_failure.description: How one step failed. code and advice are kept as the step's error carried them, so their values are open.

details.description: Structured context, such as the step that was running.

counts.description: The number of steps per outcome, plus those never reached; together they cover the planned steps.
